Customer IDs in raw_transactions show mixed case (e.g. 'c00138'), while raw_customers uses uppercase 'C00001'..'C00200'. The profile shows 361 distinct customer_ids in transactions against 200 customers, which is consistent with each id appearing in both an uppercase and a lowercase form. The case mismatch makes the join drop the lowercase rows, which accounts for 4582 vs 4264.

The fix is to normalize customer_id with upper(trim()) in silver_transactions. A normalized id should map cleanly to the 200 customers, since the max lowercase value 'c00200' is the same id space. Trimming is a small precaution in case of whitespace. The 361 distinct count is plausible for 200 ids in two cases, but I can't confirm that every id matches after upper(). If some ids still don't match, they would be dropped by the inner join, so I'm assuming they all match. gold_customer_spend would also be corrected, since it groups by the normalized id.

silver_customers is already unique per customer_id, with 200 distinct in 200 rows, so no join fan-out occurs. I'll also normalize customer_id there with upper(trim()), which doesn't change the output.

Only silver_transactions needs to change. Output columns and their meaning stay the same.
